cues.zh: 如果把铀放在氟气溶液中，它会变成六氟化铀，

cues.en: which is gaseous.
cues.zh: 这是一种气体。

cues.en: And that will just come right as a solution.
cues.zh: 这样就能直接以溶液形式出来。

cues.en: So, it was a one step process to remove the fuel that you're making from what it is that
cues.zh: 因此，去除你正在制造的燃料与将要成为燃料的物质——在此例中是钍——是一个单步过程。

cues.en: will become the fuel, in this case the Thorium.
cues.zh: 这一过程将变成燃料，也就是这里的钍。

cues.en: This trick doesn't work in Uranium Plutonium but it does work in Thorium Uranium because
cues.zh: 这个技巧在铀钚中不起作用，但在钍铀中却有效，因为

cues.en: of the particular chemical characteristics of that fuel.
cues.zh: 该燃料具有特定的化学特性。

cues.en: So again nature is--nature is kind.
cues.zh: 所以，大自然又一次——大自然是仁慈的。

cues.en: Lesson for LFTR.
cues.zh: LFTR的教训。

cues.en: The ability to separate this stuff is a big deal and you can do it at high temperatures.
cues.zh: 分离这些物质的能力至关重要，而且可以在高温下完成。

cues.en: You can do it at high radiation fields.
cues.zh: 这项工作能在高辐射场中完成。

cues.en: It's inherently chemical process.
cues.zh: 它本质上是化学过程。

cues.en: There's no cooling off that's required.
cues.zh: 不需要冷却。

cues.en: So, this got them even more excited and then serendipity struck.
cues.zh: 于是，这让他们更加兴奋，接着好运降临了。

cues.en: One day, they were meeting in 1959 and they found out the Atomic Energy Commission wanted
cues.zh: 1959年的一天，他们开会时发现原子能委员会想要

cues.en: to build experiments.
cues.zh: 建造实验装置。

cues.en: And so they had to cost less than a million dollars.
cues.zh: 而且成本必须低于一百万美元。

cues.en: The guy who did--the guy who ran the--what will be--what I'm about to explain you, the
cues.zh: 负责这个——负责运行——即将——我马上要向大家解释的

cues.en: Molten Salt Reactor Experiment, he wrote the proposal in a day.
cues.zh: 熔盐反应堆实验的那个人，一天之内就写好了提案。

cues.en: How many of you guys could write a proposal for a nuclear reactor in a day?
cues.zh: 你们中有多少人能在一天内写出一份核反应堆的方案？

cues.en: Yeah, I couldn't do it either but--all right, Chris could do it, Chris--But what happens
cues.zh: 是啊，我也做不到，不过——好吧，Chris能做到，Chris——但现实中有时会发生的情况是

cues.en: sometimes in the real world is when people wants stuff they don't want to be patient
cues.zh: 当人们想要东西时，他们不想为此耐心等待

cues.en: for it.
They want the answer right then.
cues.zh: 他们想立刻得到答案。

cues.en: They want the proposal.
cues.zh: 他们想要那份方案。

cues.en: So, you got to be ready.
cues.zh: 所以，你得做好准备。

cues.en: And to keep things simple he just wanted to simulate the core of what it was they wanted
cues.zh: 为了保持简单，他只想模拟他们想要建造的东西的核心部分

cues.en: to build.
He wanted to have it bigger.
cues.zh: 他想把它做得更大。

cues.en: He wanted to have it--have more power but there are all these limitations based on what
cues.zh: 他想让它——拥有更大功率，但受制于

cues.en: the Atomic Energy Commission wanted.
cues.zh: 原子能委员会的各种要求。

cues.en: So this is what the Molten Salt Reactor experiment looked like.
cues.zh: 这就是熔盐反应堆实验装置的样子。

cues.en: It was a bunch of graphite fuel elements in that tank and then they would flow the fluoride
cues.zh: 罐子里装着一堆石墨燃料元件，然后让氟化物

cues.en: fuel through it.
cues.zh: 燃料流过其中。

cues.en: And here it is sitting in its hot cell.
cues.zh: 这就是它放在热室里的样子。

cues.en: You can see the reactor kind of in the middle.
cues.zh: 你可以看到反应堆大致在中间。

cues.en: There's the salt pump and the heat exchangers.
cues.zh: 有盐泵和热交换器。

cues.en: So, you'd run the--you'd run the salt through the core and it would get hot and then it
cues.zh: 所以，你把盐送过核心，它就会变热，然后它

cues.en: would give up its heat to the heat exchanger and then it would all be driven by these pumps.
cues.zh: 会把热量交给热交换器，然后这一切都由这些泵驱动。

cues.en: And they ran this reactor for about five years from 1965-1969 and during that time, it demonstrated
cues.zh: 他们从1965年到1969年运行了这个反应堆大约五年，在那段时间里，它展示了

cues.en: a lot of the features that we would want ultimately in LFTR.
cues.zh: 我们最终希望在LFTR中实现的许多特性。

cues.en: Online refueling, they did it.
cues.zh: 在线加注燃料，他们做到了。

cues.en: This is actually a capsule and they would load it up with new fuel and they just dropped
cues.zh: 这其实是个胶囊，他们会装入新燃料，然后直接把它

cues.en: it in the reactor and they were just kind of--the fuels in the capsule just dissolve
cues.zh: 丢进反应堆，燃料在胶囊里就慢慢溶解

cues.en: away.
cues.zh: 掉了。

cues.en: When they wanted to take out the Uranium, they use Fluorination.
cues.zh: 当你想取出铀时，就用氟化法。

cues.en: They showed that that worked.
cues.zh: 他们证明了这方法可行。

cues.en: They could remove all the Uranium.
cues.zh: 能去除所有的铀。

cues.en: Actually did that 1968.
cues.zh: 实际上1968年就这么做了。

cues.en: And then they did a sample where they took out some of the fuel and they distilled away
cues.zh: 然后他们做了个样本，取出部分燃料，蒸馏掉

cues.en: all the good stuff out of the fuel and they just left behind the waste.
cues.zh: 燃料里所有有用的东西，只留下废物。

cues.en: So, each of these steps was really demonstrated successfully in the MSRE.
cues.zh: 所以在MSRE中，每一步都得到了成功验证。

cues.en: And they have this fantastic safety feature.
cues.zh: 而且他们还有个绝妙的安全设计。

cues.en: It's called the freeze plug.
cues.zh: 叫做冷冻塞。

cues.en: Now, because the fuel is so hot, if you cool it down it will--it will freeze.
cues.zh: 因为燃料温度极高，一旦降温就会凝固。

cues.en: And it will lock up in the pipe and so they had a little blower over a flattened section
cues.zh: 它会在管道里凝固锁死，所以他们在管道一段压扁的区域装了个小鼓风机

cues.en: of pipe and it kept--it kept part of the salt just frozen right there in the pipe.
cues.zh: 让一部分盐始终保持凝固状态，就卡在管道那里。

cues.en: So, the whole idea was if you lost all power to the reactor if you turned all the lights
cues.zh: 所以整体思路是，即便反应堆完全断电，所有灯都灭了

cues.en: off, all the juice off, all that would happen is that Freeze plug would melt and the salt
cues.zh: 所有电力都切断，后果也只是冷冻塞熔化，盐液

cues.en: would drain out into a drain tank that was passably cooled.
cues.zh: 排入一个冷却还算过得去的排放罐里。

cues.en: Now this is so cool because this reactor--in most reactors you have to take the coolant
cues.zh: 这太酷了，因为这个反应堆——在大多数反应堆里，紧急情况下你得把冷却剂

cues.en: to the reactor in an emergency situation.
cues.zh: 输送到反应堆里。

cues.en: And that makes them hard to build because you got to have the regular core be able to
cues.zh: 这让它们很难建造，因为你得让常规堆芯能够

cues.en: run and make power 99.9% of the time but in an emergency case, you got to be able to get
cues.zh: 99.9%的时间运行发电，但在紧急情况下，你得能够

cues.en: the emergency cooling in and override everything else you designed for all the other times.
cues.zh: 把应急冷却送进去，并覆盖你为其他所有时间设计的一切。

cues.en: This reactor was the complete opposite.
cues.zh: 这个反应堆完全相反。

cues.en: You could have the core just do what it was supposed to and if there was an emergency
cues.zh: 你可以让核心只做它该做的事，如果出现紧急情况

cues.en: it would send the fuel to the safe place.
cues.zh: 它就会把燃料送到安全的地方。

cues.en: It would send the fuel to the place where it was going to be passably cooled.
cues.zh: 它会把燃料送到能够勉强冷却的地方。

cues.en: So, fantastic safety feature.
cues.zh: 所以，这是极好的安全特性。

cues.en: And one of the ones that they demonstrated in the MSRE--in fact these guys on Friday
cues.zh: 而他们在MSRE中演示的其中一个——事实上，这些人周五

cues.en: afternoons they wouldn't want to leave the reactor running over the weekend.
cues.zh: 下午可不想让反应堆在周末继续运行。

cues.en: So they'd just go in and they turn off all the power and the salt plug would freeze.
cues.zh: 于是他们就走进去，关掉所有电源，盐塞就会凝固。

cues.en: The thing would drain into the tanks.
cues.zh: 东西会排入储罐。

cues.en: It would lock--it would freeze up over the weekend they'd come back on Monday.
cues.zh: 它会锁死——它会在周末冻结，他们周一回来。

cues.en: They turned the heaters on.
cues.zh: 他们打开了加热器。

cues.en: They pumped it out of the tanks back up into the core.
cues.zh: 他们把它从储罐里抽回堆芯。

cues.en: So, I mean they did this over and over, over again.
cues.zh: 所以，我是说他们一遍又一遍地这么做。

cues.en: Fantastic safety feature.
cues.zh: 绝佳的安全特性。

cues.en: Here's a picture of the building the MSRE is in today.
cues.zh: 这是MSRE如今所在建筑的照片。

cues.en: Now, that's not actually the MSRE but, uh, it's down--it's actually right below that
cues.zh: 其实那不是MSRE，但，呃，它在下面——其实就在那块

cues.en: concrete slab.
cues.zh: 混凝土板正下方。

cues.en: I was there a few years ago and--and got to see the buildings.
cues.zh: 几年前我在那儿，还看到了那些建筑。

cues.en: So if you ever get a chance to go out to Oak Ridge National Labs, you know, tell them to
cues.zh: 所以如果你有机会去橡树岭国家实验室，你知道，告诉他们

cues.en: take you over to the old MSRE building ORNL 7503.
cues.zh: 带你去旧的MSRE大楼ORNL 7503。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So lessons for LFTR from the MSRE.
cues.zh: 那么LFTR从MSRE学到的教训。

cues.en: You got to be ready to demonstrate your idea because when the time comes you're not going
cues.zh: 你必须准备好展示你的想法，因为时机到来时你不会

cues.en: to get much warning.
cues.zh: 得到太多预警。

cues.en: They're going to want the answer and a working example is worth stacks of documents and theories.
cues.zh: 他们会想要答案，而一个可行的例子胜过成堆的文件和理论。

cues.en: So, one of things I love to tell people like, you know, "How do you know this works?"
cues.zh: 所以，我喜欢跟人讲的一件事就是，你知道，“你怎么知道这行得通？”

cues.en: And I go "We'll, they did it.
cues.zh: 然后我说，“嗯，他们做过了。

cues.en: It really works."
cues.zh: 真的行得通。”

cues.en: And they demonstrated not all but most of the features that are pertinent to this reactor.
cues.zh: 他们展示了并非全部、但大部分与这个反应堆相关的特性。

cues.en: Well after doing that, they really wanted to investigate how to build the real thing
cues.zh: 做完这些之后，他们真的很想研究如何建造真正的东西

cues.en: and they began to go through different design concepts for what would be called the Molten
cues.zh: 于是他们开始研究不同的设计概念，也就是后来被称为熔盐

cues.en: Salt Breeder Reactor, The MSBR.
cues.zh: 增殖反应堆的东西，MSBR。

cues.en: Some had pebbles, some had prismatic filaments but the basic idea was that you were going
cues.zh: 有的放卵石，有的用棱柱状细丝，但基本思路是

cues.en: to have these sections in the middle that would run the core salt and you're going to
cues.zh: 中间这些区域用来运行核心熔盐，然后

cues.en: surround the whole thing with a Thorium blanket.
cues.zh: 用钍毯把整个装置包裹起来。

cues.en: Kind of like that schematic that we showed earlier.
cues.zh: 有点像我们之前展示的那张示意图。

cues.en: This was about where they--where they stopped on this--on this design.
cues.zh: 这大概就是这个设计走到的地方。

cues.en: It's a little hard to see but the fuel would get pumped up through the middle, go up to
cues.zh: 不太容易看清，但燃料会从中间向上泵送，

cues.en: the top and then come back down in an annulus.
cues.zh: 到达顶部，然后沿环形通道向下回流。

cues.en: And it--it led to a lot of plumbing problems and some very tight tolerances on graphite.
cues.zh: 这就带来了很多管道问题和石墨公差极紧的问题。

cues.en: And that was a real concern for them because they didn't know how graphite was going to
cues.zh: 这对他们来说是个大问题，因为他们不知道石墨在辐照下会

cues.en: respond under irradiation.
cues.zh: 有什么反应。

cues.en: And here's more pictures just showing what the reactor looked like in the building.
cues.zh: 这里还有更多图片，展示了反应堆在建筑里的样子。

cues.en: But the really appealing thing about this approach was they had this super simple fuel
cues.zh: 但这种方法真正吸引人的地方在于，他们有一套超级简单的燃料

cues.en: cycle.
cues.zh: 循环。

cues.en: I mean you would make the--you would make the fuel, you would fluorinate it out, you
cues.zh: 我是说，你会制造——你会制造燃料，把它氟化提取出来，你

cues.en: would introduce it to the core, you'd burn it up.
cues.zh: 会把它送入堆芯，然后烧掉它。

cues.en: When it was time to reprocess the core, you take out the fuel, you distill off the good
cues.zh: 到了处理核心燃料的时候，你把燃料取出来，提炼出有用的

cues.en: stuff and you were just left with fission products.
cues.zh: 部分，剩下的就只是裂变产物了。

cues.en: So, it was just a super simple closed nuclear fuel cycle.
cues.zh: 所以，这就是一个超级简单的闭式核燃料循环。

cues.en: Here it is in--in more schematics.
cues.zh: 这里用更多示意图来展示。

cues.en: I'm--I'm going to leave all these slides, make them available to you so you can peruse
cues.zh: 我会把这些幻灯片都留下来，提供给你们，方便你们

cues.en: these at your leisure.
cues.zh: 闲暇时仔细查看。

cues.en: A lot of these things I'm, I'm flying through because we don't have a lot of time.
cues.zh: 很多事情我都讲得比较快，因为我们时间不多。

cues.en: But I want you to, to get an idea for the depth of the work they did.
cues.zh: 但我想让你们了解一下他们所做工作的深度。

cues.en: Now, the real problem they had was with graphite.
cues.zh: 现在，他们真正的问题出在石墨上。

cues.en: Graphite would swell--or first it would contract and then it would swell under irradiation.
cues.zh: 石墨会膨胀——或者先收缩，然后在辐照下膨胀。

cues.en: And as they began to realize this they thought, "A lot of our plans for how we were going
cues.zh: 当他们开始意识到这一点时，他们想：“我们关于如何建造这个反应堆的很多计划

cues.en: to build this reactor aren't going to work just because of tolerancing and how graphite
cues.zh: 都行不通了，仅仅是因为公差以及石墨

cues.en: is going to change."
cues.zh: 会如何变化。”

cues.en: and so forth.
cues.zh: 等等。

cues.en: So, they had to--they had to move away from the two-fluid reactor, it had a plumbing problem.
cues.zh: 所以，他们不得不——他们不得不放弃双流体反应堆，因为它存在管道问题。

cues.en: So, for us we got to realize that the plumbing problem's got to be understood and managed.
cues.zh: 所以，对我们来说，我们必须认识到管道问题需要被理解和管理。

cues.en: And I--I think it can be, I have some really good ideas with that.
cues.zh: 而且我——我认为这是可以做到的，我对此有一些非常好的想法。

cues.en: But the overall appeal of the two-fluid reactor is still great and it really comes from that
cues.zh: 但双流体反应堆的整体吸引力仍然很大，而这确实源于

cues.en: very, very simple fuel cycle.
cues.zh: 非常非常简单的燃料循环。

cues.en: Well, after the two-fluid they moved to a one-fluid and it's like they traded one set
cues.zh: 嗯，在双流体之后，他们转向了单流体，这就像是他们用一组

cues.en: of problems for another.
cues.zh: 问题换来了另一组问题。

cues.en: Now, the Thorium and the Uranium were mixed together in one fuel.
cues.zh: 现在，钍和铀混合在同一种燃料里。

cues.en: The core was a lot simpler it was just these--it was actually very, very simple.
cues.zh: 核心部分简单多了，就只是这些——实际上非常简单。

cues.en: It was just these prismatic fuel elements of graphite--I'm sorry not fuel elements,
cues.zh: 就只是这些棱柱形的石墨元件——抱歉，不是燃料元件，

cues.en: prismatic elements of graphite.
cues.zh: 是棱柱形的石墨元件。

cues.en: You'd pump the salt in the bottom, it would flow up through all the graphite elements
cues.zh: 你把盐从底部泵入，它会向上流过所有石墨元件

cues.en: and then it would be pumped up out the top.
cues.zh: 然后从顶部被泵出。

cues.en: So, it was a very, very simple reactor design.
cues.zh: 所以，这是一个非常非常简单的反应堆设计。

cues.en: Unfortunately the simplicity in the reactor led to complications in the reprocessing.
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，反应堆的简化导致了后处理的复杂化。

cues.en: The reprocessing went from being easy to hard.
cues.zh: 重新处理从容易变得困难。

cues.en: And the basic reason for that is it's very difficult to separate Thorium from the fission
cues.zh: 而根本原因在于，很难将钍与裂变产物分离

cues.en: products.
cues.zh: 产品。

cues.en: They chemically are very similar.
cues.zh: 它们在化学性质上非常相似。

cues.en: In the two-fluid approach, the Thorium wasn't mixed with fission products because fission
cues.zh: 在双流体方案中，钍没有与裂变产物混合，因为裂变

cues.en: wasn't taking place where the Thorium was.
cues.zh: 反应并不在 Thorium 所在的位置发生。

cues.en: The Thorium's in the blanket, the Uranium is in the core.
cues.zh: 钍在包壳里，铀在堆芯里。

cues.en: It's easy to separate Uranium from fission products, it's hard to separate Thorium.
cues.zh: 把铀从裂变产物中分离出来很容易，分离钍却很难。

cues.en: So, that's why it got complicated.
cues.zh: 所以，这就是为什么它变得复杂了。

cues.en: So, a lesson for LFTR, fixing one problem can create another and the other problem you
cues.zh: 所以，LFTR 的一个教训是，解决一个问题可能会制造另一个问题，而

cues.en: create often is bigger than the first.
cues.zh: 制造出的另一个问题往往比第一个更大。

cues.en: So, maybe we should be thinking about a two-fluid reactor, everybody who's on my forum knows
cues.zh: 所以，也许我们应该考虑双流体反应堆，我论坛上的每个人都知道

cues.en: that I'm a big advocate for the two-fluid reactor.
cues.zh: 我是双流体反应堆的坚定支持者。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Well, if you want to have a reactor that is fairly compact, you have to think a little
cues.zh: 那么，如果你想要一个相当紧凑的反应堆，你就得稍微想一想

cues.en: bit about, "Why are reactors not so compact today?"
cues.zh: “为什么今天的反应堆不那么紧凑？”

cues.en: And this shows what a containment structure looks like in a typical light water reactor.
cues.zh: 这展示了典型轻水反应堆的安全壳结构是什么样的。

cues.en: Here's the reactor which, although it's big, is not nearly as big as the containment structure.

cues.en: The reason that containment is so big is because the water in the reactor--if the reactor is
